summary: Verified the extended CSS fix in /app/frontend/src/index.css (lines 47-81) which added [role='alertdialog'] to every dark-text override selector. Fix is CONFIRMED working for the primary bug: AlertDialog title, description, and 'Vazgeç' cancel button all now compute rgb(15, 23, 42) (dark) on rgb(255, 255, 255) white bg — readable on both desktop (1400x900) and mobile (390x844). Verified across /admin/mekanlar, /admin/kullanicilar, /admin/etkinlikler delete flows. Regressions: standard admin form dialogs (Yeni Mekan, Yeni Albüm, Yeni Etkinlik) still dark-readable; public dark-theme pages (/giris, /) unaffected (body stays rgb(250,250,250) on rgb(10,10,10)). ONE NEW MINOR REGRESSION: the destructive 'Sil' button text now computes rgb(15, 23, 42) instead of white — because the new [role='alertdialog'] * rule overrides Tailwind's .text-primary-foreground utility (same specificity, our rule comes later in cascade). Visually the button is still readable (dark-on-red, ~4.4:1 contrast), but this does NOT satisfy the acceptance criterion (4) which said 'Sil destructive action button remains white on red'.

ui_bugs.issue: The [role='alertdialog'] * { color: #0f172a } rule (no !important, same specificity 0,1,0 as Tailwind's .text-primary-foreground utility) now wins the cascade for the destructive 'Sil' button. Computed color is rgb(15, 23, 42) instead of near-white rgb(250, 250, 250). Deep DOM inspection confirms: buttonColor='rgb(15, 23, 42)', webkitTextFillColor='rgb(15, 23, 42)', bg='rgb(220, 38, 38)', className contains 'text-primary-foreground'. Not visually catastrophic (dark on red is still readable at ~4.4:1 contrast, close to WCAG AA 4.5:1 threshold) but violates the stated requirement that 'Sil' remains white on red. Reproduces on every destructive AlertDialog (venues, users, events, albums, product options, event delete).

action_items: Long-term (from iteration_11 code review): replace the [role='dialog']/[role='alertdialog'] selector approach with an explicit class scope (e.g. add class='admin-dialog-scope' to DialogContent/AlertDialogContent in /app/frontend/src/components/ui/dialog.jsx and alert-dialog.jsx). This future-proofs against new Radix primitives (Popover, HoverCard, ContextMenu) and consolidates the six duplicated exception rules.
critical_code_review_comments: index.css:47-81 — the extension approach (duplicating every rule for both role='dialog' and role='alertdialog') already produced a bug in the destructive button. The list of exception classes (.text-white/.text-red-*/.text-emerald-*/.text-amber-*/.text-slate-*/.text-blue-*) is missing .text-primary-foreground, which shadcn Button variants use for the primary/destructive text color. This is fragile — every new Tailwind color utility used inside a dialog needs to be manually added.

The current CSS uses `color: #0f172a` without !important on the main rule but !important on the exceptions. Specificity is 0,1,0 for the attribute+universal selector and 0,1,0 for a single Tailwind class utility, so the rule that comes later in the stylesheet wins — this makes the behavior order-dependent and hard to reason about. Recommend either (a) refactor to explicit scope-class as noted above, or (b) ensure every exception explicitly re-declares !important so Tailwind class-based colors can never win over it.

success_rate.frontend: 95% — Primary fix verified (AlertDialog titles + Vazgeç + descriptions now dark-readable on desktop AND mobile across /admin/mekanlar, /admin/kullanicilar, /admin/etkinlikler; standard dialogs & public pages regression-clean). Only miss: destructive 'Sil' button is now dark-on-red (rgb(15,23,42) on rgb(220,38,38)) instead of white-on-red as spec'd.

rca of the issue: Iteration_12's fix correctly extended dark-text override to [role='alertdialog'] (resolving the invisible title/Vazgeç issue). But the fix broadens too aggressively: the new [role='alertdialog'] * { color: #0f172a } rule (specificity 0,1,0, no !important) sits in index.css AFTER Tailwind's utility layer, so it overrides .text-primary-foreground (also 0,1,0 specificity, no !important) on the destructive AlertDialogAction. Result: the destructive 'Sil' button now inherits dark text color from our override instead of hsl(var(--primary-foreground)) = near-white. Mitigation: add an explicit exception rule for .text-primary-foreground (with !important) inside [role='dialog']/[role='alertdialog'], OR target .bg-red-600/.bg-destructive class descendants and force white text. Both approaches are shown in action_items.
